svg.font-family: system-ui, -apple-system, 'Segoe UI', Roboto, Helvetica, Arial, sans-serif
svg.title: What the refrigerant phase-out means for existing and new HVAC systems
svg.desc: With an R-410A system, keep using it: R-410A stays available for repairs, though prices are expected to rise gradually as they did for R-22. A new system already uses R-32, common in ductless mini splits and many residential systems, or R-454B, common in ducted systems; both meet the EPA's 700-GWP limit.
svg.text: What the phase-out means for you
Keep using it; nothing forces a replacement
gradually, as they did for R-22
It already uses a new refrigerant:
R-32, common in ductless mini splits
Both new refrigerants meet the EPA's 700-GWP limit for new equipment.
